::: {.unit unit="lp-breacher"}
The breacher carries demolition charges for walls and turrets. Against units the charges do little, and a breacher alone dies quickly. Send breachers in behind troopers and aim them at the pillboxes first.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-trooper"}
The trooper is your basic soldier: heavy armor and a submachine gun, and the cheapest unit on the command link. Troopers beat raiders, scouts and Shotgun hands and lose to long-range lasers, so send them in numbers. Only a powered barracks heals them.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-rocket-trooper"}
The rocket trooper's rockets are made for armor and fliers; against troopers they are no better than a rifle. It takes more of the command link than a trooper and outranges a Heavy tank's rail cannon. Keep rocket troopers behind your troopers against infantry, and in front against tanks and drones.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-battle-tank"}
The battle tank fires a slow, heavy shell. It takes the longest to train and the most bandwidth. Its shell is made for buildings, so it is the tool for a walled camp and a poor one against crowds. Keep troopers with it.
:::

::: {.unit unit="lp-flame-trooper"}
The flamethrower trooper has the shortest range and the most damage of your infantry. It burns biter swarms and bunched squads quickly but does little to vehicles, and nearly everything outranges it. Lead with it against Synthexis and keep it at the back against Kessler-Hayashi.
:::
